claims.statement: CLI configuration selects WebhookValidator for validator type webhook and JsonPatchWebhookMutator for mutator type json_patch_webhook; the exported full-job WebhookMutator is not selected by createMutator and has no supported HCL type.

Webhook configuration requires a webhook block, an absolute HTTP(S) URL with a host, and a nonblank method accepted by http.NewRequest, without a POST-only restriction; configured adapter constructors validate endpoints but defer method syntax errors to invocation.
Configuration validates controller names as nonblank and unique within each kind, runs validation on load and server build, and exposes only endpoint and method in the Webhook configuration block.

All three webhook adapters serialize the shared Payload containing the entire current api.Job under job and optional RequestContext under context, rather than sending an AdmissionReview, bare job, or Nomad registration envelope.

All webhook adapters use the configured method and endpoint, set Content-Type and Accept to application/json, and attach X-Forwarded-For and NACP-Client-IP for nonempty context ClientIP and NACP-Accessor-ID for nonempty AccessorID.
The proxy derives context ClientIP from the first incoming X-Forwarded-For entry or RemoteAddr, without independently authenticating the forwarded value.

resolve_token requested by any controller enables pipeline-wide token resolution on actionable admission requests using Nomad /v1/acl/token/self; missing tokens can leave tokenInfo absent even when resolveToken is true.

Webhook identity context contains a sanitized ACLTokenContext without SecretID, and fresh webhook requests do not forward the incoming X-Nomad-Token; this does not sanitize the full job content sent to the policy service.

Admission mutators run sequentially before validators, feeding each result into the next mutator and stopping on errors; validators receive copies of the final job and accumulate errors across sequential invocations.
Original request context is passed through admission controller spans into NewRequestWithContext for each webhook, allowing cancellation and deadlines to terminate outgoing work.

WebhookValidator decodes errors and warnings string arrays: empty or omitted arrays accept, warnings without errors are returned, and nonempty errors become a multierror with nil warnings even if warnings coexist.

JsonPatchWebhookMutator expects a patch/warnings/errors envelope, converts warnings first, and rejects nonempty policy errors before applying a patch by returning nil job, false mutation flag, warnings and an aggregated error; a regression test guards policy-error rejection.

JSON-Patch operations apply to the serialized job rather than the Payload wrapper, and PatchJob decodes/applies operations and unmarshals the result into api.Job; mutated is based on nonempty operations rather than semantic inequality, and an omitted or empty patch is a no-op.

Patch decoding, application, or result decoding failures return nil job, false mutated, nil warnings and an error; AdmissionMutators also drops warnings when any mutator returns an error, including warnings retained by the patch adapter on policy denial.

The full-job WebhookMutator takes a URL pointer without parsing validation, decodes a bare replacement api.Job response rather than a policy envelope, reports mutation with reflect.DeepEqual, and returns no warnings.

Each webhook invocation creates a client with a 30-second timeout using a shared package-level instrumented transport over http.DefaultTransport; otelhttp installs otelhttptrace beneath transport spans, and webhook clients do not use the separately configured Nomad backend TLS transport.

All webhook adapters return request construction, marshaling, and transport errors without an adapter-level retry loop, and defer response body closure after successful Client.Do on all subsequent result paths.
DecodeJSONResponse reads at most 10 MiB plus one byte, reports read errors before rejecting responses over 10 MiB, then rejects statuses outside 200–299 before JSON unmarshaling.

Webhook response decoding uses json.Unmarshal without checking Content-Type or rejecting unknown object fields; empty bodies, malformed JSON, trailing non-whitespace data and incompatible field types fail, so an empty 204 response is not a valid policy result.
Webhook clients install no custom redirect policy, so status validation applies to the response delivered by Go's client rather than necessarily the initial response.
Common request, transport and response decoding failures return nil warnings and an error from WebhookValidator, and nil job, false mutated, nil warnings and an error from both webhook mutators.

Registration and planning admission failures reach the proxy HTTP 500 error path without forwarding; validation mutation failures also return immediately, but validator errors are stored and merged into Error and ValidationErrors on successful Nomad validation responses rather than always producing an immediate HTTP rejection.
The demo uses service-discovered HTTP webhook endpoints marked testing-oriented, and MockHooks serves empty warnings/errors on /validate and an additional empty patch on /mutate.

httptest adapter tests exercise validator payload decoding, methods, paths, headers and results, JSON-Patch no-ops, patches, invalid operations, policy rejection and status errors, and full-job replacement and context headers; remoteutil contract tests cover endpoint parsing, headers, transport type, size, status, malformed JSON and read failures.
